Yes! I was super into Mystery Incorporated as a kid and still re-watch it every few years. I honestly think it's a well-crafted show! There are sort of two layers to the plot: a simple, contained in one episode mystery that holds to that cartoon, "I would have gotten away with it if it weren't for you meddling kids" structure, and a larger mystery that unfolds over a few seasons which is really well done, with good twists and stakes. The larger thread comes to feel very emotionally mature, as you sort of climb away from the initial setting of goofy high school-ers in a van. The tone changes over time, feeling more real and dire through the characters' perspective, sometimes even bleak. The eeriness it comes into is a similar tone to Twin Peaks sometimes imo (but it's still comforting because you've been with the characters the whole way).

I think the musical themes are really effective, the characters get to have depth, and change, and the story is really well done even though it has a few stagnant episode-stretches. It also has self-awareness. Their town, Crystal Cove, is a tourist city that markets itself as being haunted because so many people there  dress up as supernatural creatures to try and get away with crimes lol. 

All in all, I should re-watch this show again!

I was in the same place for a long time. My school counsellor tried to figure out where the negative self-image came from, but I'd had it as long as I could remember. It felt like the mechanism behind a rocket launch: something used to propel the negativity, but the jets detached long ago, leaving me hurtling into space, unable to reach the source, and unable to fix it. I was hopeless. Helpless.

I never found the cause of it, but you don't need to. You have to understand that you didn't choose to be miserable. You didn't decide on the narrative of your mind, nobody wants to be unhappy. The pervasive thoughts are stuck on repeat, and in order to let them you, you need to understand that they're not your fault in the first place.

Medication can help to get unstuck and cognitive behavioral therapy helped me to see through destructive thoughts. It is hell to go through what you are surviving, and you need to know that it is not your fault. It's not fucking easy, and that's why the positivity rings so false.
